summary: Dry-run #2 plan stage closes all four dry-run #1 high-severity REV-L2 findings by construction. REV-L2-001 (buyerEmail wire) is encoded across identity.profile.read (first-class customer-JWT contract), checkout.commit step 2 (forwarded Bearer JWT), and order.create-from-checkout (required+email-bound buyerEmail field with VALIDATION_ERROR failure mode); REV-L2-002 (env-var split) is encoded as a single accepted INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET name with startup-fatal rejection of INTERNAL_SECRET / SHARED_SECRET / SVC_SECRET; REV-L2-003 (constant-time compare) mandates crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare and forbids ==/!= with a documented Reviewer grep pattern; REV-L2-004 (compound stub dead-end) is acknowledged in ADR-007 plus connectivity.md failure_modes with the canonical sole-writer entry-point order.cancel-on-checkout-failure made a real handler. The plan ships eight components, 57 contracts, and ten ADRs. One blocking medium remains: components.json incorrectly lists nine admin-only contracts as frontend-web dependencies even though BA EPIC_FRONTEND and connectivity.md both lock admin to backend-only (curl/Postman). This will misdirect Tech-Designer's fan-out scope. Three low-severity advisory items round out the review.

findings.locus: components.json#/components[component_name=frontend-web]/dependencies and complexity_rationale (claims '36+ contract surfaces ... every customer + admin endpoint'); contradicted by ba.json#/out_of_scope[0] ('Admin web UI ... Admin remains backend-only via Postman/curl in MVP'), EPIC_FRONTEND.md L10/L26/L71/L92 ('no admin UI ... so Tech-Lead does not invent admin pages downstream'), and connectivity.md L100-108 ('Admin endpoints (CUSTOMER-token-rejected): Admin (curl/Postman, no UI)')
findings.description: components.json#/components[frontend-web]/dependencies includes nine admin-only contracts (catalog.product.create, catalog.product.update, catalog.product.soft-delete, catalog.category.create, catalog.category.update, catalog.category.deactivate, inventory.stock.adjust, order.list-admin, order.update-status-admin) that no STORY_FRONTEND_* file validates and that EPIC_FRONTEND explicitly puts out of scope. The complexity_rationale's '36+ contract surfaces (every customer + admin endpoint plus 6 cross-cutting contracts)' claim is inflated by these nine and contradicts the BA scope-cut that the EPIC author flagged as 'the single biggest interpretive call versus runs/01'. Tech-Designer reading components.json verbatim will scope frontend-web route-handler stubs for admin endpoints with no story-level AC backing them, wasting fan-out cycles and risking a scope-creep Reviewer-L1 cycle later.
findings.recommendation: Drop the nine admin contract names from frontend-web.dependencies and revise the complexity_rationale to 'every customer endpoint + 6 cross-cutting' (count: 30 deps). Frontend-web stays complexity=complex on its remaining cookie-Bearer translation + Idempotency-Key + customer-journey integration burden — the tier does not need the admin endpoints to justify itself.

findings.locus: contracts.json#/contracts[name=order.create-from-checkout]/side_effects and request.buyerEmail wording ('persisted as buyer_email_snapshot on order_items snapshot block')
findings.description: buyerEmail is a per-order field but is documented as denormalized onto every order_items row rather than onto the orders row. ADR-001 (schema-per-service) justifies snapshot denorm broadly, and the rationale 'support order.list-admin search-by-email' is plausible if admin search reads order_items, but the denorm width (N rows per order each carrying the same email) is unusual and not load-justified in MVP. Risk is small: a Dev who interprets literally will produce more storage and more writes per checkout than necessary; a Dev who normalizes to orders.buyer_email_snapshot will produce a cleaner schema but diverge from the contract.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether buyerEmailSnapshot lives on orders (one row per order) or order_items (N rows per order). The orders-row placement is the cleaner default; if order_items placement is intentional for an admin search hot-path, name that requirement explicitly in the contract notes.

findings.locus: EPIC_CHECKOUT/STORY_CHECKOUT_COMMIT.md#/acceptance_criteria — no AC names buyerEmail resolution, even though contracts.json makes buyerEmail a required field with a VALIDATION_ERROR failure mode
findings.description: The REV-L2-001 fix is fully encoded at the contract layer (checkout.commit step 2 and order.create-from-checkout.buyerEmail), but the customer-facing AC in STORY_CHECKOUT_COMMIT does not surface 'the buyer's email is persisted on the order from the authenticated user's profile' as a verifiable behavior. A QA-L1 author tracing only the story file would not write a test that asserts the order carries the customer's identity-side email. Internal data-flow can be considered out-of-scope for customer-AC, but adding one AC would close the trace gap and harden the dry-run-#1 regression posture.
findings.recommendation: Add an AC to STORY_CHECKOUT_COMMIT: 'Given an authenticated customer with profile email E, when checkout commit succeeds, then order detail's persisted buyerEmail equals E (REV-L2-001 fix; CHK-007).'

findings.locus: ba.json#/acceptance_criteria — admin PAID->PACKING->SHIPPED->DELIVERED happy-path is covered only implicitly via the order.detail AC (line ~229-231) and success_conditions; STORY_ORDER_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS.md/acceptance_criteria lists only two negative cases (SHIP-without-tracking, DELIVERED->cancel)
findings.description: STORY_ORDER_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS's title is 'Admin moves PAID -> PACKING -> SHIPPED -> DELIVERED' yet its AC block only validates two negative cases (VALIDATION_ERROR on missing tracking, INVALID_ORDER_STATE on DELIVERED cancel). The happy-path assertion (each forward transition succeeds, status_history rows are written, trackingNumber persists on SHIPPED) is implicit in the title and in BA success_conditions but not in the story's AC list. A QA-L1 reading this story alone may miss the happy path. Not blocking because contracts.json#/order.update-status-admin/transitions is fully specified and the BA success_conditions name the path explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Add an AC to STORY_ORDER_ADMIN_TRANSITIONS that asserts the three forward transitions succeed and that each writes a status_history row carrying actor=ADMIN; tracking number is stored on SHIPPED.
